prompt: Why does the shop's budget notify rather than stop resources?
hint: What would switching off do to checkout?

choices.text: Budgets are not allowed to touch resources
choices.why: The reason given is about outcomes, not permissions.

choices.text: Stopping would turn a cost problem into an outage
choices.why: Right. People decide; the budget tells them.

choices.text: Notifications are cheaper than actions
choices.why: Cost is not the argument.

choices.text: Because the budget is illustrative
choices.why: The amount is illustrative; the design is not.

prompt: Match each budget notification to when it is most useful.
hint: Actual looks back; forecast looks ahead.

pairs.right: An early warning, with time to act

prompt: A change on the 9th adds 9 USD a day. Why might the budget's 80% notification not help?

choices.text: Budgets ignore Log Analytics
choices.why: They include every cost in their scope.

choices.text: The notification only fires on the last day
choices.why: It fires whenever the threshold is passed.

choices.text: It arrives days late, if it arrives
choices.why: Right. Budgets catch the month, not the day something changed.

choices.text: 9 USD is under the budget's minimum unit
choices.why: There is no such unit.

prompt: series_decompose_anomalies flagged no day in the sixty. What does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: Nothing unusual happened to the bill
choices.why: The daily table shows a clear step on the 9th.

choices.text: The emulator's function is broken
choices.why: It ran and scored every day; the step was absorbed.

choices.text: This step slipped past it
choices.why: Right. A detector is as good as the change it is built to see.

choices.text: The threshold of 2.5 should be raised
choices.why: Raising it would flag even less.

prompt: Before the anomaly function can run, the daily rows are turned into an array by the operator ___.
hint: Lesson 10 named it; it has a hyphen.

prompt: Why does the daily check use the median of fourteen days rather than the average?

choices.text: One odd day does not move the median
choices.why: Right. The baseline stays steady.

choices.text: Kusto cannot average a join
choices.why: It can; the choice is about robustness.

choices.text: The median is always lower, so more days are flagged
choices.why: It is not always lower; robustness is the point.

choices.text: Cost Management exports only medians
choices.why: Exports hold daily costs, not statistics.

prompt: For how many days in a row did the rule flag the step, starting on the 9th?
The flag stopped on the 17th although nothing was fixed. Why does the lesson call that its most important line?
hint: What did the median contain by then?

choices.text: Because it proves the debug logs were turned off
choices.why: Nothing was turned off; the cost stayed high.

choices.text: Because the 5% threshold was crossed downwards
choices.why: The cost did not fall; the baseline rose.

choices.text: Because the export stopped on the 17th
choices.why: It continues to the 18th.

choices.text: The new level became the usual: the window to act closed
choices.why: Right. Letting the flag sit a week accepts the cost.

prompt: Which meter moved, according to which.kql?

choices.text: SQL Database
choices.why: It moved by under a dollar.

choices.text: Log Analytics
choices.why: Right. From 28 to 89 USD a week.

choices.text: Virtual Machines
choices.why: Not in the top three changes.

choices.text: Storage
choices.why: It moved by cents.

prompt: Put the investigation of the cost step in order.
items: which.kql names the meter: Log Analytics
The Usage table names the table that grew
The activity log shows the setting that changed
trap: Starting from the activity log is the slip: without the meter, every change of the week is a suspect.

prompt: Which actions did the shop take after the cost step? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A DCR transformation that drops Debug traces in production
choices.why: Yes. Dropped rows are never billed.

choices.text: An expiry date on temporary log-level changes
choices.why: Yes. A debug level cannot be forgotten on.

choices.text: A lower budget for rg-shop
choices.why: No. The budget was not what failed.

choices.text: Removing Log Analytics from the shop
choices.why: No. The workspace is how the shop sees anything.
